entries.title: a module exports its C bindings
entries.body:
An `export declare function` and an opaque `export declare class X {}` can now be imported by name from another module, so one generated binding module can serve the others. An importer calls an exported binding under the same buffer, count and escape rules as its own declaration, and `ffi` is charged to every module that calls it. entries.title: refuse a new u32-cast wrap and spell intended wraps with nish:unsafe
entries.body:
* ci: refuse a new u32-cast wrap and spell intended wraps with nish:unsafe

A sum cast through u32 and back, toI32(toU32(a) + toU32(b)), makes signed
arithmetic wrap without the compiler proving it fits, so it can hide a panic
and nobody reading it can tell whether the wrap was meant. CLAUDE.md now says
a wrap is spelled, never cast: a wrap that would hide an overflow becomes a
proven sum or a Result, and one the algorithm means is wrappingAdd,
wrappingSub or wrappingMul from nish:unsafe. The WP80-WP87 rules, WP83's
wrapping-sum note and docs/AI.md say the same.

scripts/wrap-casts.mjs, in npm run lint, finds each such cast in std/, src/
and examples/ (i32 and i64 forms, any spacing or line break, comments
blanked) and checks it against scripts/wrap-casts.txt, the 555 casts in 69
files from before the rule. A count may only fall: a new cast fails and
names every cast in its file, and a fall fails until --update writes it back.

* docs: plan WP91, taking every u32-cast wrap in std/, src/ and examples/ to zero

WP91 sweeps the 555 cast wraps scripts/wrap-casts.txt pins, in seven
stages by area, each cast becoming a proven sum, a Result, or a
nish:unsafe wrapping call, then drops the baseline so the lint allows
none. Filed as #2359 at the top of the Roadmap, ahead of WP80.

entries.title: read multipart/form-data bodies in nish/net/multipart
entries.body:
nish/net/multipart reads a multipart/form-data body (RFC 7578, on RFC 2046's
multipart syntax) one part at a time.

A MultipartReader walks a body against its boundary and gives each part's
name, filename, content type and the byte range of its data. It refuses a
body that breaks the syntax or a MultipartLimits cap (parts, header bytes,
header lines), and refuses when the final delimiter is missing.

For one-off reads there are three calls, each a reader with the default
limits over the whole array:
- multipartPartCount counts the parts, or answers a negative refusal code.
- multipartFieldData gives the named field's bytes.
- multipartFieldFilename gives the named field's filename.

The module lands spec-first: contracts/multipart-form-data.json holds 21
requirements, 18 properties and 5 vectors quoted from RFC 7578 and RFC 2046.
Its security record is docs/security/multipart.md.

Tests: tests/link/net_multipart, test/spec/multipart-form-data.ts
Refs: docs/guide/using-nish/http-server.md, docs/security/multipart.md

entries.title: RSA-PSS CertificateVerify under an RSA certificate on the TLS and QUIC servers
entries.body:
* feat(runtime): constant-time RSA-PSS signing under a Secret key (WIP)

nish/crypto/rsa-sign parses a PKCS#1 RSAPrivateKey of 2048 to 4096 bits
into a Secret, and signs RSASSA-PSS with SHA-256 by a fixed 4-bit window
over Montgomery arithmetic whose final subtraction is chosen by mask. Each
signature is checked against the public exponent before it is returned.

Refs: RFC 8017 §8.1.1, §9.1.1

* feat(runtime): split RSA key arithmetic from salted signing; TLS key signer

Moves the key parser and Montgomery arithmetic into nish/crypto/rsa-key,
which reaches no randomness, and leaves the salt-drawing signers in
nish/crypto/rsa-sign. TlsKeySigner dispatches CertificateVerify signing on
the configured scheme; TlsTcpServer signs through it.

Refs: docs/security/crypto-rsa.md

* feat(runtime): derive the RSA-PSS salt from the key in nish/crypto/rsa-sign

Merge the key parser and the signer into one module, nish/crypto/rsa-sign,
and derive the 32-byte PSS salt as SHA-256(label || d || mHash), as P-256
derives its nonce under RFC 6979. Nothing reaches crypto.getRandomValues, so
the module compiles for wasm32 and has no io-exit panic site. The private
exponent is copied out with expose, hashed in the caller's scratch and wiped
with the hasher, the shape p256SignSha256Into has. TlsRsaSigner bounds the
key size with literals before it sizes the signature.

* feat(runtime): load RSA keys from PEM and sign HTTP/3 handshakes by the configured scheme

x509ParseRsaPrivateKey reads a PKCS#1 "RSA PRIVATE KEY" or a PKCS#8
"PRIVATE KEY" holding rsaEncryption into a Secret for nish/crypto/rsa-sign.
Http3Server now signs its CertificateVerify through TlsKeySigner, so a QUIC
config whose signatureScheme is rsa_pss_rsae_sha256 serves an RSA certificate.

Refs: std/crypto/x509.ts, std/net/http3-server.ts

* test(runtime): serve an RSA-2048 certificate to openssl, curl and a QUIC client

tests/link/net_tls_rsa_server loads the PKCS#1 and PKCS#8 forms of an
RSA-2048 key, refuses a 1024-bit one, completes TLS 1.3 handshakes whose
CertificateVerify is rsa_pss_rsae_sha256 and checks it under the
certificate's key, refuses a hello offering only ECDSA, and answers an
HTTP/3 GET over QUIC under the RSA leaf. tests/run.js runs the same program
as an HTTP/1.1 and an HTTP/2 server over TLS for openssl s_client and curl.

Tests: tests/link/net_tls_rsa_server

* feat(runtime): record RSA-PSS signing, with Wycheproof vectors, a ct_asm fixture and a wipe check

The RSA-PSS signer the TLS and QUIC servers use under an RSA certificate
gets its security record: docs/security/crypto-rsa.md covers
std/crypto/rsa-sign.ts and x509ParseRsaPrivateKey (RSA-S1 to RSA-S6), and
tls.md and http3.md describe RSA-PSS CertificateVerify. The raw private
operation is checked against Wycheproof's RSA-2048, -3072 and -4096 keys,
and PSS signing against known answers that OpenSSL verifies. ct_asm checks
the reduction, the Montgomery product and the window step for secret
branches and addresses, and a -O2 count pins the signer's wipes. The guide
shows how to serve an RSA certificate and key.

Tests: tests/link/crypto_rsa_sign, tests/link/crypto_rsa_sign_f64, tests/cases/ct_asm_rsa
Refs: docs/security/crypto-rsa.md#rsa-pss-signing

* docs(runtime): name the Wycheproof files the RSA signing keys come from, and record the untested 2049-bit encoding

crypto-rsa.md said the signing tests' keys came from crypto_wycheproof_rsa;
they come from Wycheproof's rsa_pkcs1_{2048,3072,4096} decryption files,
read by generate.mjs. RSA-S6 now also records that no test key has a bit
length one more than a multiple of 8, the case where the PSS encoding is a
byte shorter than the modulus. x509ParseRsaPrivateKey's doc comment no
longer claims the key must be a whole number of bytes: any odd modulus of
2048 to 4096 bits loads.

Refs: docs/security/crypto-rsa.md#method-signing

* test(runtime): declare the IR that RSA-PSS CertificateVerify under an RSA certificate moves in nish-cmp

The TLS stack now links nish/crypto/rsa-sign (and through it
nish/crypto/hmac), and TlsTcpServer and Http3Server hold a TlsKeySigner
where they held a TlsP256Signer. Each program and module that moves is
declared by name: 290 new rsa-sign.ll or hmac.ll modules, 26 programs whose
tls.ll, http2-tls.ll or net_http3_peer.ll lay out the new signer, five
wasm32 loaders whose storage global is renumbered, and the three new
programs that the seed refuses because it has no nish/crypto/rsa-sign.

Tests: tests/nish-cmp.js

* fix(runtime): pin RSA key wipes and check HTTP/3 for RSA-PSS CertificateVerify under an RSA certificate

Round-1 review of the RSA server signer. The opt -O2 wipe check now pins
x509ParseRsaPrivateKey's key-block wipes and rsaParsePrivateKey's, with
TlsKeySigner.sign making no key copy. net_tls_rsa_server drives the
HTTP/3 listener on the RSA pair with OpenSSL's s_client -quic where the
installed OpenSSL has it, and records a skip where it does not. The
peer-signature match accepts OpenSSL 3.5's rsa_pss_rsae_sha256 spelling.
rsaSignKeyBits keeps its leading-zero test behind a bound the panic
prover reads, and the RSA and TLS docs state what the signer checks.

Tests: tests/link/net_tls_rsa_server, tests/link/crypto_rsa_sign

* test(self): regenerate the httparena golden after merging main

* fix(runtime): list nish/crypto/rsa-sign as a std module for RSA-PSS CertificateVerify under an RSA certificate

src/std-modules.ts and the user guide's module table name the new
nish/crypto/rsa-sign module, the guide's x509 row names
x509ParseRsaPrivateKey, and crypto_rsa_sign links under --profile speed
like the other programs whose wipes a check counts. A doc comment in
rsa-sign.ts is rewrapped.

Tests: tests/link/crypto_rsa_sign

* test(runtime): link crypto_rsa_sign and its f64 twin through SPEED_LINK, not args

tests/speed-link.txt sets the speed profile for the RSA signing programs, so their args no longer name one. The QUIC half's missing refusal check is recorded as untested in the TLS and HTTP/3 records.

* perf(runtime): sign with CRT, checked, for RSA-PSS CertificateVerify under an RSA certificate

The RSA private operation is now two half-size fixed-window exponentiations,
by dP mod p and dQ mod q, joined by Garner's formula, in place of one
exponentiation by d mod n. Every signature is still raised to e and compared
with its input before it is returned, which is what stops a faulty half from
leaking a prime (the Bellcore fault). A key's CRT values are checked when it
loads: p and q odd, dP < p, dQ < q, qInv < p, p q = n and q qInv = 1 mod p,
then a trial signature under the CRT path and one under d. The per-prime
Montgomery constants are computed once at load and kept in the key's
Secret, which grows to 4 k + 9 w bytes. Every limb array that held a prime,
a half exponent or a half signature is wiped, and the new arithmetic is under
the constant-time assembly check on x86-64, aarch64 and x86-64-v3.

Adds the spec-first contract for RFC 8017 RSASSA-PSS with SHA-256
(specs/, contracts/, test/spec/), whose checks cite their clauses, and
rsaVerifyPssDer for it to verify under a DER public key.

Measured: 2048-bit sign 15.6 ms -> 4.1 ms (3.8x), 3072-bit 55.1 -> 13.3 ms (4.1x), 4096-bit 131.6 -> 31.3 ms (4.2x); medians of 5 interleaved rounds of 30 signs, about +-10%, verify-after-sign included
Refs: docs/security/crypto-rsa.md
Tests: tests/link/crypto_rsa_sign, test/spec/rfc8017-rsassa-pss-sha256.ts, tests/cases/ct_asm_rsa

* chore(scripts): list rsa-sign's RFC 6979 and x509's RFC 8017 as cited

The PSS salt's comment names RFC 6979 for how it is derived, and x509 names
the PKCS#1 key that rsa-sign parses under its RFC 8017 spec; neither file
implements the RFC it names.

* fix(runtime): discharge rsa-sign's five unproven indexes for RSA-PSS CertificateVerify under an RSA certificate

The CRT form's 2 c-limb loops kept a bounds check the prover could not
discharge (NL9007 under the performance gate): each now runs c limbs and
reaches the upper half as c + l, and the key's span check runs to the span
list's length. The work still depends on the key size alone.

Tests: tests/cases/ct_asm_rsa

* test(runtime): declare the TLS layout moves main's new h1 TLS and h2c programs show for RSA-PSS CertificateVerify under an RSA certificate

Fifteen programs main added since the last sync link the TLS stack, so they
write rsa-sign.ll and lay out TlsKeySigner where the seed laid out
TlsP256Signer.

* test(runtime): format the RSA-PSS CertificateVerify under an RSA certificate declarations

* test(crypto): sign RSA-PSS against NIST CAVP, OpenSSL, Go and pyca

The RSA-PSS signer now has to reproduce signatures it did not compute
itself: NIST CAVP's 30 FIPS 186-2 SHA-256 signatures under its 2048, 3072
and 4096-bit keys, and 50 signatures under ten keys that OpenSSL, Go's
crypto/rsa and pyca/cryptography made, with odd sizes (2049, 2050, 2054,
3071, 4094 bits) and exponents of 3, 65537 and 2^32 - 1. Each key loads
from the PKCS #1 DER and the PKCS #8 PEM its library wrote, and both loads
sign every case byte for byte. Five keys outside 2048 to 4096 bits, or with
e of 2^32 or more, must be refused by both parsers.

The 2049-bit key closes RSA-S6, the PSS encoding when emLen is one byte
shorter than the modulus: setting emLen to k fails five of its cases.
Removing the e < 2^32 guard fails the refusal check.

Tests: tests/link/crypto_rsa_sign_interop

* fix(crypto): prove every index and size in the RSA signer

std/crypto/rsa-sign.ts is a new std/ module, and a new module may have no
panic site the compiler cannot prove away. The CRT rewrite left nine: the
key-buffer size in rsaSignKeyBytes, a span-length subtraction in
rsaParsePrivateKey, and the window-table index in rsaSignWindowStep and
rsaSignPow.

Each one now has a range test the prover reads. The size restates
rsaSignHalfWidth's bounds, a span refuses a negative end as well as a
negative start, and the table index is tested against the table's length.
That test is always true after the length test at the top of the function.
It is on public values only, and ct_asm still finds no secret branch in the
window step.

Tests: tests/cases/ct_asm_rsa

* fix(self): regenerate the goldens and reference for the first-form RSA key

The merge of main brought a known-answer spec that hands rsa-sign keys of
RFC 8017's first form; the goldens and the library reference follow the
module, and the security record names the route.

* docs(security): name the first-form exponentiation in RSA-S2

RSA-S2 now lists rsaSignFullOp and rsaSignPow, and records that
rsaSignPow's table build and nibble loop, which both signing routes
run, are not in the constant-time fixture.

entries.title: a std class owns its native handles, is exported, and closes with using
entries.body:
A handle class may now own several native fields (CPtr, an opaque declare class, HostHandle<K>, or another handle class), each optionally `| null` except HostHandle. Each field is readonly and written once at the top of the constructor. `using` closes them in reverse declaration order, then closes owned child handles. Handle classes and the functions that take them can be exported from a library module and lent across modules. A top-level factory may return H, H | null or Result<H, E>. Each method call is still one field load plus the direct C call.

New refusals: NL2825 (a write to an owning field that is not a move), NL2826 (an argument that may leave after a `new` has taken ownership of a handle), NL2827 (an entry module exporting a handle). Library-module handle functions are left out of --emit-header, --emit-dts and --emit-napi.

entries.body:
* refactor(runtime): prove std/net/url.ts sums instead of casting them to wrap

WIP for WP91 S4: the URL parser's cast wraps become sums the bounds prover
discharges, so a window or escape past the array is refused, not wrapped.

* refactor(runtime): type urlLowerString's width so --number-mode f64 compiles it

A literal 0 in a ternary is f64 under --number-mode f64, so the width is an
i32 local set under the guard instead.

* refactor(runtime): prove the HTTP/1 codec, server, serve and prefork sums instead of casting them to wrap

Offsets in the HTTP/1 codec go through saturating helpers the bounds prover
proves; clock sums in the server, serve and prefork add same-sign magnitudes
in u64 and hold the result below 2^63, exact on every reachable input.

* refactor(runtime): prove the HTTP client, its response codec and the outbound filter sums instead of casting them to wrap

Window ends go through a checked helper whose refusal takes the codec's
existing error, digit accumulators stay u64 under their existing caps, and the
response generation counter, compared only for equality, wraps by wrappingAdd.

* refactor(runtime): prove the HPACK, HTTP/2 and protobuf sums instead of casting them to wrap

HPACK table and index arithmetic become ordered differences the bounds prover
proves, with an out-of-range dynamic index taking the existing reject path;
HTTP/2 clock and flow-control sums hold at the i64 range's ends; protobuf's
zigzag stays unsigned; HPACK's copied-octets statistic, read only as a
difference, wraps by wrappingAdd.

* fix(runtime): spell the wraps in std/net fields, static, compress, upstream, handler and server

The cast wraps in the HTTP field codec, the static file server, the response
compressor, the upstream pool, the handler and the HTTP server become sums the
prover proves under the parse's existing caps, or saturating clock helpers.
No peer-reachable value changes.

* test(runtime): regenerate the checked goldens for the std/net HTTP wraps

* refactor(runtime): keep serveTask's line where the pinned negative names it

* test(runtime): declare the httparena IR moves of std/net HTTP, HPACK, URL and the server stack

* docs(runtime): point the handler record at handlerCheckLimits's moved lines

The handler record's std/net/handler.ts line references named lines that had moved; they now name the guard's panic, openHttpHandler's fault check and its constructor call where they stand.

* perf(runtime): keep the HTTP/1 field and section scans at main's cost

The field-line and section scans write the sums their guards bound plainly
and keep http1Past and http1Less for the rest, so the bounds prover
discharges them without a clamp in the loop.

* perf(runtime): write the HTTP/1 section's line sums plainly

* perf(runtime): take the HTTP/1 request-line marks and writer ends as exact sums

The request-line marks, the response writer's byte copies and the request
line's length cap now add offsets whose range the code has already checked,
in place of a clamped i64 sum per call, and urlPortOf keeps its port in a
ranged lane.

* refactor(runtime): format the HTTP/1 name guard and drop the unread port constant

* test(self): regenerate the goldens for the HTTP/1 and URL sum rewrites

Every corpus program reaching nish/net/hpack, http2-tls, protobuf or
http-compress gets a narrow declaration per moved file, measured against
the 0.49.1 seed.

is now u32 like the rank it is built from, and the constructor counts
each length in it, so neither needs a cap test. hpackWindowEnd takes
off + len in i64 with one compare, and hpackCheckWindow's panic moves
into its own function so the check inlines. std-net-http2-frame is back
at main's count.

* perf(runtime): inline the HPACK window check, its panic kept apart

inlines; hpackCheckWindow holds only the panic, so std-panics keeps it
as the one kept site it was.

entries.title: explicit baseline raises in bench/instructions.json
entries.body:
No instruction baseline can rise without a recorded entry. `node bench/run.mjs --instructions --update` refuses to write a count more than the tolerance above its baseline unless `--raise <row> --why "..."` names that row. A named raise is appended to a new `raises` array in bench/instructions.json as `{row, from, to, why, pr}`. A row with no stored count is new and needs no raise.

scripts/instruction-raises.mjs <base.json> <head.json> compares two baseline files. It prints a base/head/change table, which also goes to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY when that is set. It uses the smaller of the two tolerances, so a head cannot widen its own band. It fails on a raise that has no new matching entry, on a row the head keeps without its count, and on any file whose counts are not positive integers.

Tests: tests/fixtures/instruction-raises, node tests/run.js instruction-raises

Part of #2440

entries.title: the byte getters check their window through one guard callers can prove

Each fixed-width getter and setter in std/bytes.ts checks its whole window once, first, through bytesWindow, a guard in the shape the window contract records, and panics with a literal message naming the function and its width. A caller whose own test holds the window, such as `off >= 0 && off + 4 <= b.length` before a getU32LE, now proves the call and builds without --allow-panics; an untested call still lists one unproven site. entries.title: a caller's proof discharges a std callee's contract panic
entries.body:
* fix(checker): a caller's proof discharges a std callee's contract panic (WIP)

A function or method whose leading statements are if (test) { panic(m) } on
comparisons of its own parameters holds those tests as a contract site at
each call, proven where the caller proves every comparison false.

Refs: #2296

* fix(checker): a caller's proof discharges a std callee's contract panic

A function or method whose first statements are `if (test) { panic(m) }`
on its own parameters holds those tests as a `contract` site at each call,
proven where the caller's arguments make every comparison false. When every
call into the callee is proven, its panic is listed proven, so a root
program's call into std that proves the guard builds under --deny-panics.
One call nothing proves leaves the panic the callee's.

Tests: tests/cases/deny_panics_caller, tests/link/caller_contract_proven, tests/link/caller_contract_unproven

* test(self): regenerate the checked goldens for the caller contract

* test(self): declare the caller-contract flips in nish-cmp

The two new cases compile under the candidate and are refused by the seed,
which still keeps a proven caller contract's panic.

Tests: tests/cases/deny_panics_caller, tests/link/caller_contract_proven

* fix(checker): a caller's proof discharges a std callee's contract panic across forwards, fields and modules

A caller contract is read only from the module that defines the callee, so an
importer's listing of a signature no longer marks it seen before its home
module records the contract (std's routerDecode lost its contract that way),
and a forward reads its target from the target's own module, which may come
later in the program list. Method guards, field initializers and `new` in a
field read the caller's proof too, and a re-export keeps the contract.

Each exclusion holdCallerContracts keeps has a case that fails without it;
the tag, hidden-reference and dispatcher exclusions are gone, subsumed by the
value cases.

Tests: tests/link/caller_contract_*

* test(checker): drop caller-contract nish-cmp entries main's merge settles

After merging main, hpack, the quic-* modules and record.ll agree between the
seed and the candidate for both httparena programs, and record.ll does for
net_handler_pipelined_stream, so their caller-contract declarations go.

* fix(checker): a call into a caller contract no one holds lists no contract site

A call whose callee's contract is not held (a window shape #2403 does not
read as a guard, or a holder whose own target is dropped) kept a proven
contract entry beside its call-through-panic entry. The fixpoint now drops
such holders and their contract sites, so each call site is one or the other.

The guards the prover could not read in the caller-contract loops are spelled
so it reads them (no new NL9007), and the http1-codec guide example, which
now builds strict, loses its --allow-panics opt-out.

Tests: tests/link/window_contract_not_a_guard, tests/link/window_near_dropped

* test(checker): pin that a panic guard no caller proves stays the callee's

The caller-contract rule proves a leading `if (test) { panic(m) }` guard
when every call into its function proves the test false. A new link case,
tests/link/panic_caller_unproven, pins the other half: a guard whose one
call passes a value read from the command line stays unproven, and the call
lists `call` via `panic`. It fails if the rule holds a contract an unproven
call reaches. docs/LANGUAGE.md's `panic` row now names both cases.

Tests: tests/link/panic_caller_unproven

* test(checker): regenerate panics_panic for the caller-proof rule

`checked(21)` is a call into a leading `panic` guard its caller proves
false, so its panic is now proven and the call lists a proven `contract`
site. The golden is rewritten from the compiler's output and the header
names the case that keeps the unproven half.

Tests: tests/cases/panics_panic

entries.title: prove or remove the std panic sites relay reaches
entries.body:
* fix(net): make h3CheckWindow a window guard so callers prove it away

h3CheckWindow now has the window-guard shape, so a caller that proves its
window removes the panic site, and WebTransport.close, sendDatagram and write
forward the proof to their callers. Http3FrameHeader.read is the forwarding
form of h3ReadFrameHeader, and WebTransport's own capsule writes test their
windows where the prover sees them.

Tests: tests/link/net_http3_frame

* fix(runtime): prove the base64 decoders' output allocations

base64urlDecode and base64StdPadDecode sized their output with an inline
`u32` product the bounds prover could not read, so each allocation was a
checked length that panics on overflow. Both now size it as the sum of two
non-negative `i32` locals, at most three quarters of the text's length, which
the prover discharges: strict callers of either decoder no longer reach a
panic site in them.

Tests: test/spec/rfc4648-base64.ts

* fix(net): prove the HTTP/3 frame and server windows relay reaches

h3CheckWindow takes the window guard's shape, so a caller's window over its
own buffer is a window site the prover discharges, not the one panic inside
the guard every caller reached. Http3FrameHeader.read checks its window and
reads through h3FrameHeaderIn; Http3Server's receive hands udpRecvFrom the
whole receive buffer, its length bounded by a literal the prover reads. The
std-panics baseline records the exported forwarders' guard calls the
root-package sweep keeps, and docs/security/http3.md says why.

Tests: tests/std-panics.json, link/net_http3_frame_bad_window

* docs(net): regenerate the http3-frame reference for Http3FrameHeader.read

The reference moves with the new public method's doc comment.

* refactor(net): drop webtransport's unused h3ReadFrameHeader import

The capsule header reads through Http3FrameHeader.read now.

* fix(net): give webtransport's zero window starts an i32 local

A bare 0 is an f64 under --number-mode f64, and the prover does not read WT_ZERO, a module constant; a typed local is both an i32 and a literal it proves.

Tests: link/net_webtransport_f64, link/net_relay_f64

* docs(net): say WebTransport.write panics on a window outside its buffer

The guard now runs before the stream lookup, so a bad window panics even
for a stream this layer does not hold.

* test(net): declare the HTTP/3 frame IR moves of the std panic sites relay reaches

h3CheckWindow's window-guard shape and Http3FrameHeader.read move
http3-frame.ll, http3.ll and the modules that declare the header's
methods in 31 corpus programs; no program flips between refused and
compiled.

* test(self): regenerate the checked goldens for the std panic sites relay reaches

* docs(net): regenerate the webtransport reference for WebTransport.write

* docs(net): record the entropy exit and WebTransport.write's window check

WebTransport.write checks its window before it looks up the stream, so a
window outside `buf` on a stream this layer does not hold now panics where
it used to answer H3_CLOSED; its doc comment says so. The HTTP/3 record
gains H3-10: a failed entropy read in the server's `build`/`unowned` exits
the process, and no caller can carry a Result because the builtin has no
failure answer. tests/std-panics.json is regenerated after taking in main.

* docs(net): cite H3-10 from the HTTP/3 security index row

* fix(runtime): clear std panic sites relay reaches in qpack and p256 hashing

WIP: qpack whole-field encode, sha256 absorb without the finished check for a fresh hasher, p256Mac over sha256Wiped.

* refactor(runtime): keep hmac and qpack window checkers off the forwarder contract

A checker turned into a window guard makes every forwarding method a
host-judged window site in its own module, which raised the per-kind
counts; the relay path past hmac's begin still stops at Sha256.update.

* fix(runtime): hash RFC 6979's HMAC through a fresh absorbed Sha256

p256Mac takes its two hashers from sha256Absorbed, which absorbs the
parts into a fresh hasher past update's finished check, so signing
reaches no Sha256.update panic; p256Mac still wipes both hashers, as
before. carryEnd hands writeData a local zero the window prover reads.

* fix(runtime): drop sha256's unused wipe import

* test(runtime): lower http-server's window count and move qpack's kept panic

carryEnd's local zero clears one window site, so the ratchet falls 1055 to 1054.
qpack's range panic now lives in qpackPushStreamCancellation.

* perf(runtime): keep Sha256.update a single absorb call

The window and finished checks move into sha256Absorb, which reports a
refused window as false, so update stays one call and one test on the HMAC
hot path; encodeLine's arguments at qpack.ts go one per line.

* perf(runtime): write SHA-256's padding as a zero run and one 0x80 byte

digestInto zeroed the block after the message one byte at a time, choosing 0x80
or 0 per byte; zeroing the run and then writing the 0x80 byte lets it lower to a
fill, which pays for the window check moving into sha256Absorb. update keeps its
finished check and its two panics.

* docs(runtime): build the key-distrust example under the default

pkiDistrustSpki's example reaches no std panic site now that sha256.ts
proves its windows, so its --allow-panics marker and the note above it go.

* fix(net): answer H3_INVALID for a write window outside its buffer

Http3Connection.writeStream, writeData and writeDataWhole, and
WebTransport.close, write and sendDatagram, refuse a window that does not
lie inside its buffer with H3_INVALID, before the stream or session is
looked at, rather than panicking. Each was an exported forwarder of
h3CheckWindow, so each kept an unproven window site of its own.

Tests: tests/link/net_http3_write_window, tests/link/net_webtransport_stream_window

* fix(net): record the HTTP/3 writes' H3_INVALID window answer

The std-panics ratchet falls to 1028, and the HTTP/3 record states that a
write's window outside its buffer answers H3_INVALID, not a panic.

* docs(net): regenerate the reference for the H3_INVALID windows

* test(net): declare qpack.ll's move under examples-strict S8

qpackPushInteger takes its prefix as a literal mask and a u64 and no
longer panics, so qpack.ll moves in the twenty corpus programs that link
the HTTP/3 stack.

* test(net): declare qpack.ll's move in the rest of S8's HTTP/3 programs

entries.title: WebSocket on the nish/net/http-server façade's HTTP/1.1 listener
entries.body:
* feat(runtime): WebSocket on the nish/net/http-server façade's HTTP/1.1 listener

WIP: HttpServer.acceptWebSocket, sendFrame, received and closeWebSocket over
the HTTP/1.1 carrier's WebSocket slot; a held message is the decoder's buffer,
handed to the program through take, with no copy.

Fixes #2011

* test(runtime): cover the façade's WebSocket in tests/link/net_http_server_ws

An echo program on `HttpServer.listenHttp1` upgrades with `acceptWebSocket`
and echoes text, a 300000-byte fragmented binary message, and a burst a
non-reading client stalls on `H1_AGAIN` and resumes on `writable`. It closes
from either side (1000), closes an unmasked frame with 1002 and a dropped
connection with 1006, reuses a pool of one request, keeps `Arena.used()` flat
over 200 warmed round trips, refuses the upgrade on h2c and on a GET without
`Upgrade` (`H1_INVALID`, answered 400), and keeps a WebSocket open past a
1 ms `bodyTimeout`.

The façade's doc comments now point at `Http1Connection` and
`nish/net/websocket` for the WebSocket rules they follow instead of citing
RFC 6455 and RFC 8441, which the façade does not implement.

Tests: tests/link/net_http_server_ws

* ci(interop): run Autobahn against the façade's WebSocket echo server

The interop job's autobahn lane now runs every fuzzingclient case against a
second server, agent nish-facade on port 9002:
tests/link/net_http_server_ws/autobahn.ts, which is the net_http_server_ws
rig. It upgrades every request through HttpServer.acceptWebSocket, takes
messages of up to 16 MiB, and echoes each one in 16 KiB fragments with
sendFrame. The interop image builds it as /ws-facade-server. The job checks
both agents' verdicts and keeps both servers' logs.

Tests: tests/link/net_http_server_ws

* docs(runtime): WebSocket on the façade's HTTP/1.1 listener

The security record gains HTTPSRV-26 to HTTPSRV-29: the upgrade only on
HTTP/1.1, the request handed back on every end, idleTimeout rather than
bodyTimeout, and the pool WebSockets can hold, recorded open. Each row
cites the check that fails when its guard is removed. The design note
gains §2.6 and the test table, and the user guide a WebSocket section
with an echo server. A test now pins that idleTimeout closes a quiet
WebSocket with 1006 and hands its request back.

Tests: tests/link/net_http_server_ws

* docs(runtime): regenerate the http-server reference for the WebSocket notes

Tests: node scripts/gen-reference.mjs --check

* fix(runtime): clear a held WebSocket message when the socket closes

A WebSocket that closed while the program held a message still answered
`message`, so its `messageData` could point into a connection buffer the
pool hands to the next connection. Closing now clears it. The record and
the guide name the decoder's close codes 1007 and 1009 beside 1002, and
the record's notes add two cases no check drives yet.

Tests: tests/link/net_http_server_ws

* test(self): regenerate the checked goldens for the WebSocket close fix

* refactor(runtime): simplify the façade's WebSocket paths and rig

A slot whose program holds a WebSocket message no longer asks for a read
wakeup, so the server does not spin while the program works on it. The
three WebSocket calls share one ownership check, the "programs" states
have one predicate, and the test rig takes the interop echo's slots,
config and fragment size instead of copying them.

Tests: tests/link/net_http_server_ws

* test(runtime): cover WebSocket over TLS and the held pool on the façade

Adds a listenHttp1Tls case to net_http_server_ws (upgrade, echo, close),
pins that a second handshake waits while a WebSocket holds a pool of one
and is upgraded once it closes, runs interop on the ws link paths, and
corrects the records' citations and scope row.

Tests: tests/link/net_http_server_ws

* fix(runtime): answer WebSocket misuse on the façade with H1_INVALID, not a panic

sendFrame, closeWebSocket and acceptWebSocket on the nish/net/http-server
façade now answer H1_INVALID on a request that is not a WebSocket the
program holds (never upgraded, or handed back), and sendFrame answers it to
a window outside its buffer; received does nothing there. The window is
summed in i64 and guarded so src/bounds.ts proves it, so std-panics holds
the module's counts as before.

Tests: tests/link/net_http_server_ws

* test(interop): declare the WebSocket program nish-cmp's seed refuses

tests/link/net_http_server_ws reads HttpServerRequest.socket and calls
HttpServer.acceptWebSocket, which the seed's std/net does not have, so only
the candidate compiles it; nish-cmp declares that exit difference under the
stage's release-note words, as it does the HTTP/1.1 over TLS programs.

Tests: tests/nish-cmp.js

* fix(interop): type sendFrame's window guard under both number modes

`sendFrame` compared an `i32` against `buf.length`, which `--number-mode f64`
types as `f64`; it now casts the length as the façade's other window guards
do. The guide's WebSocket sample makes its router with `routerChecked`, so its
own code builds under the default no-panic rule, and the explain-layout
expectation for the request-slot bench follows `HttpServerRequest`'s line and
size.

* fix(runtime): a draining http-server façade upgrades no WebSocket

acceptWebSocket now answers H1_INVALID on a draining server. The carrier's
accept cleared the close-after mark drain had set on the connection, so a
handshake read during a drain became a WebSocket the drain could not end.
The program answers the request with a status, and its connection closes.

The façade's tests also send a handshake with no Sec-WebSocket-Key and one
for version 8. The test client now looks for a response head before it
reads the peer's end, since one turn can read both.
